english: I'm not sure where the gate is.
tip: -ㄴ지 embeds a question: 어디인지 (eodi-inji) = where it is.

target: 이 짐은 기내에 들고 탈 거예요.
english: I'll carry this bag on board.
tip: 들고 타다 (deulgo tada) is literally 'hold and board' – Korean chains two verbs where English says 'carry on'. 들고 탈 거예요 (deulgo tal geoyeyo) = I'll board holding it.

english: I came to do some sightseeing.
tip: -러 marks purpose of going: 관광하러 (gwangwanghareo) = in order to sightsee.

english: I'll be here about a week.
tip: 정도 (jeongdo) = about, roughly: 일주일 정도 = about a week.

english: Where is baggage claim?
tip: -는 곳 = the place where: 짐을 찾는 곳 (channeun got) = baggage claim.

english: You can go to Korea visa-free.
tip: 무비자 (mubija) = visa-free: 무- means "without".

english: The visa is valid for three months.
tip: Months of duration use Sino numbers: 삼 개월 (sam gaewol) = 3 months.

english: I'll study for one semester.
tip: 동안 (dongan = for/during) comes AFTER the time span, not before: 한 학기 동안 (han hakgi dongan) = for one semester, literally 'one semester during'.

english: My host mother cooks well.
tip: Elders take -세요: 잘하세요 (jalhaseyo) shows respect.

english: Class starts at nine in the morning.
tip: Clock hours take native Korean numbers: 아홉 시 (ahop si) = nine o'clock. Minutes switch to Sino-Korean numbers, so a single time of day mixes both counting systems.

english: I study at the library after class.
tip: 후에 = after: 수업 후에 (sueop hue) = after class.

english: The teacher speaks slowly.
tip: Some verbs have a full honorific replacement, not just a polite ending: for a teacher, 말하다 (malhada = to speak) becomes a different verb – 말씀하세요 (malsseumhaseyo).

english: I'll register for next semester too.
tip: -(으)ㄹ게요 is a promise: 등록할게요 (deungnokalgeyo) = I will register.

english: The culture is very different from Korea's.
tip: 'Different FROM' uses the with-particle in Korean: 한국하고 달라요 (hangukago dallayo) = different from Korea, literally 'different with Korea'.

english: The way people greet is different.
tip: A verb + -는 방법 (-neun bangbeop) = 'the way of doing it': 인사하는 방법 (insahaneun bangbeop) = the way of greeting. The describing verb comes before 방법, not after.

english: I was surprised the shops close early.
tip: -아서 gives a cause: 닫아서 (dadaseo) = because it closes.

english: The local food suits my taste well.
tip: 입에 맞다 (ibe matda) is literally 'fits the mouth' – food that suits your taste 'fits'. 입에 잘 맞아요 (ibe jal majayo) = it suits me well.

english: I felt frustrated because I couldn't communicate.
tip: 말이 통하다 (mari tonghada) is literally 'words get through' – communication as an open channel. 안 통해서 (an tonghaeseo) = because they don't get through.

english: I really miss my family.
tip: Korean expresses missing a person as wanting to see them: 보고 싶어요 (bogo sipeoyo) = I want to see (them) = I miss them. The everyday 'I miss you' is literally a wish to see.

english: My mom misses me a lot.
tip: 3rd-person feelings take -어하다: 그리워하세요 (geuriwohaseyo) = (she) misses.

english: My younger sibling wonders how I am.
tip: Others' curiosity uses -어하다: 궁금해해요 (gunggeumhaehaeyo).

english: When I miss home, I look at photos.
tip: -(으)ㄹ 때 = when: 그리울 때 (geuriul ttae) = when I miss it.

english: I make sure to watch Korean news every day.
tip: 챙기다 (chaenggida = look after) chained before another verb adds 'make sure to': 챙겨 봐요 (chaenggyeo bwayo) = I make a point of watching, not just watch.

english: I want to eat the kimchi stew my mom makes.
tip: -고 싶다 = to want to: 먹고 싶어요 (meokgo sipeoyo).

english: As time passed it got a little better.
tip: -(으)니까 = as/since: 지나니까 (jinanikka) = as time passes.

english: My family says they'll come visit soon.
tip: -ㄴ대요 relays what was said: 온대요 (ondaeyo) = (they) say they'll come.

english: It took time to adjust.
tip: -는 데 = for the task of: 적응하는 데 (jeogeunghaneun de) = to adjust.

english: I write letters to my parents often.
tip: 께 (kke) is the respectful version of 에게 (ege = to): 부모님께 (bumonimkke) = to my parents. The particle itself carries the politeness.

english: Whenever things are hard I think of my family.
tip: -ㄹ 때마다 = every time: 힘들 때마다 (himdeul ttaemada).

english: I was very nervous since it was my first trip abroad.
tip: -이라서 (-iraseo) after a noun means 'because it is': 첫 해외여행이라서 (cheot haeoeyeohaeng-iraseo) = because it's my first trip abroad – no separate word for 'is' needed.
